title: OpenTelemetry Distributed Tracing, Collector Pipelines & Context Propagation
summary: Master cloud-native distributed tracing with OpenTelemetry (OTel): configuring OTel Collector pipelines (receivers, processors, exporters), W3C tracecontext distributed header propagation across microservices, tail-based sampling, and validating collector configs using otelcol.
learningObjectives: Understand W3C TraceContext standards (traceparent, tracestate) and distributed context propagation across asynchronous boundaries.
Configure OpenTelemetry Collector pipelines with memory_limiter and batch processors, validating configs with otelcol.
Implement tail-based sampling strategies in OTel Collector to capture error and high-latency traces while dropping mundane traffic.

curriculumModules.title: Distributed Tracing Foundations & W3C TraceContext Propagation
curriculumModules.conceptSummary: Distributed tracing correlates operations across microservice boundaries. The W3C TraceContext standard defines the traceparent header: version, 16-byte trace-id, 8-byte parent-span-id, and trace-flags. Passing this header across HTTP/gRPC requests allows backends (Jaeger, Tempo) to reconstruct end-to-end DAG execution trees.
curriculumModules.productionArchitecturePattern: Mandate W3C TraceContext propagation across internal service meshes and API gateways, ensuring asynchronous message queues (Kafka, RabbitMQ) forward trace headers in message metadata.

curriculumModules.title: OpenTelemetry Collector Architecture & Pipeline Engineering
curriculumModules.conceptSummary: The OpenTelemetry Collector receives telemetry in multiple formats (OTLP, Zipkin, Jaeger), processes it through ordered pipeline processors (memory_limiter, batch, transform), and exports to backends. Ordering is critical: memory_limiter must precede the batch processor to prevent out-of-memory crashes during traffic surges.
curriculumModules.productionArchitecturePattern: Deploy OTel Collector in dual-tier architecture: node-level DaemonSets for lightweight agent forwarding, sending to an autoscaled Gateway deployment for tail-sampling, enrichment, and egress fan-out.

labs.title: Authoring and Validating OTel Collector Pipelines with otelcol
labs.scenario: Configure enterprise telemetry ingestion: author an OpenTelemetry Collector configuration in /otel/collector-config.yaml defining otlp receiver (protocols: grpc, http), memory_limiter and batch processors, and otlp exporter pointing to tempo:4317. Wire these under service.pipelines.traces. Validate the configuration using otelcol validate --config=/otel/collector-config.yaml, then deploy as ConfigMap otel-collector-config in namespace monitoring.
labs.productionContext: Pre-validating OTel Collector configurations prevents invalid processor orderings or missing receiver definitions from crashing the collector fleet in production.
objectives: Deploy ConfigMap otel-collector-config in namespace monitoring.
labs.starterManifest:
receivers:
  otlp:
    protocols:
      grpc:
      http:
processors:
  memory_limiter:
    check_interval: 1s
    limit_percentage: 75
  batch:
    timeout: 1s
exporters:
  otlp:
    endpoint: "tempo.monitoring.svc.cluster.local:4317"
    tls:
      insecure: true
service:
  pipelines:
    traces:
      receivers: [otlp]
      processors: [memory_limiter, batch]
      exporters: [otlp]

        traces:
          receivers: [otlp]
          processors: [memory_limiter, batch]
          exporters: [otlp]
EOF

troubleshootingGuide.problem: otelcol reports configuration validation failed or ConfigMap missing.
troubleshootingGuide.cause: Receivers, processors, or exporters were referenced in service.pipelines but omitted from root definitions.
troubleshootingGuide.solution: Verify receivers.otlp, processors.memory_limiter, and exporters.otlp are defined in /otel/collector-config.yaml.

labs.title: Implementing W3C TraceContext Propagation Specifications
labs.scenario: Define distributed context propagation standards: write a JSON specification to /otel/trace-context.json defining W3C traceparent structure (version: '00', sample trace_id: '4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736', parent_id: '00f067aa0ba902b7', flags: '01'). Deploy this contract in Secret trace-context-contract in namespace default.
labs.productionContext: Standardized W3C traceparent headers allow polyglot microservice fleets (Go, Java, Node, Python) to pass distributed context seamlessly across HTTP gateways.
objectives: Apply Secret trace-context-contract in default namespace.
Verify trace_id and traceparent header presence.
labs.starterManifest:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: trace-context-contract
  namespace: default
data:
  trace-context.json: |
    {
      "header": "traceparent",
      "version": "00",
      "trace_id": "4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736",
      "parent_id": "00f067aa0ba902b7",

    }

assessmentQuestions.question: In OpenTelemetry Collector pipeline configuration, why is processor ordering critical, specifically regarding memory_limiter and batch processors?
options: Processors are executed in alphabetical order regardless of YAML definition.
The memory_limiter processor must precede the batch processor so that incoming telemetry batches are dropped or backpressured before memory is allocated for batch queues, preventing OOM crashes.
The batch processor must always run first to decompress gzip payloads.
Processor order only matters when exporting metrics to Prometheus.
assessmentQuestions.explanation: Processors execute in the exact order listed in service.pipelines. Placing memory_limiter first ensures memory checks occur before large batches are queued into memory, shielding the collector process from OOM crashes.

assessmentQuestions.question: What four fields compose the W3C traceparent HTTP header (e.g. 00-4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736-00f067aa0ba902b7-01)?
options: version (00), 16-byte trace-id, 8-byte parent-span-id, and 8-bit trace-flags (e.g. 01 recorded).
assessmentQuestions.explanation: W3C traceparent standard format is 'version-traceid-parentid-traceflags'. Version is '00', trace ID is 32 hex chars (16 bytes), parent span ID is 16 hex chars (8 bytes), and trace flags bit 0 indicates if the trace was sampled.
